$comment: What THIS product actually enforces of cockpit-ui, rule by rule.
Deliberately NOT identical to the sibling's. The contract document is family law
and is byte-identical; this file is the honest local record, and the two products
are at different stages. An empty `enforced_by` with a real `why` is a truthful
entry, not a gap to be papered over — a style guide that is wrong about itself is
The contract document never names a test. That is why this file exists.

CUI-THEME-3.why: The blocking pre-paint script and the store now resolve identically by construction (both treat key-absence as system), but nothing asserts the two agree — they are still edited independently.

CUI-THEME-4.why: The store applies the class through its environment and the test asserts it; that index.css's dark variant keys off the same class is held by the css itself.

CUI-THEME-5.why: Sign-out is a navigation and no test drives it. The funnel now reads the ck-cockpit-theme cookie, so clearing it on logout would flash the operator's own login page — this clause is now load-bearing and still ungraded.

CUI-MARK-1.why: The build-time meta injection is not written yet. Until it is, this product declares no contract version and no token digest to a browser, which is exactly the blindness that let mcp-auth-v2 carry a hand-typed marker across four repos.

CUI-MARK-2.why: The shell renders no `data-cockpit-ui` attribute yet, so a screenshot or a cross-product probe cannot tell which contract this console implements.

CUI-LOAD-4.why: The three states are each checked; that they render VISIBLY differently from one another is graded by reading source. This is the rule the four-states section exists for and it is the one nothing holds.

CUI-A11Y-5.why: Aspirational. UI-UX.md has said so in as many words since the review that found it credited to two files asserting no such thing.

CUI-AI-1.why: The assistant renders model output as chat, where no health-or-confirmation token applies. The rule binds this product only once structured model output lands in a card.

CUI-AI-2.why: pages/assistant.tsx shows no model identity or generation time today.

CUI-AI-3.why: Elicitations carry their own context; free-text turns state no provenance and nothing checks it.

CUI-AI-4.why: Elicitation approval posts to /v1/assistant/elicitations/{id}, so the affordance does record the answer — but nothing asserts the pair is absent where no endpoint exists.
